claims.text: The local catalog models the Quick Starter Gift Set Green Deck as released on December 4, 1998, as a child lane inside the Quick Starter Gift Set product.
Bulbapedia describes Quick Starter Gift Set as a two-deck kit containing a Red Deck and a Green Deck.
The local Green Deck catalog models one 60-card deck with 32 unique catalog rows; the parent rollup preserves the green lane rather than deduplicating by card name.
Bulbapedia frames Quick Starter cards as reprints from Vending Machine / Expansion Sheet material, while the local catalog preserves the Green Deck as a child lane with its own row order.
The local symbol-status matrix marks the Quick Starter parent product as printing without rarity symbols and identifies Base-overlap trainer traps, including Pokemon Trader.
Lower-tier collector research warns that Quick Starter trainer reprints without rarity symbols can be mistaken for Japanese Base No Rarity cards, especially when text/layout differences are ignored.
The local Green Deck attention rows include Mewtwo, Chansey, Bulbasaur, Scyther, Moltres, and Pokemon Trader.
The local Green Deck artist clusters include Atsuko Nishida, Keiji Kinebuchi, Aya Kusube, Sumiyoshi Kizuki, Kagemaru Himeno, Ken Sugimori, Mitsuhiro Arita, and others.

The Green Deck matters because it shows Quick Starter's gentler half: Bulbasaur ecology, fire/psychic pivots, Mewtwo and Chansey collector gravity, and the same missing-symbol trainer discipline that makes the parent product so important to agentic identification.

not_claiming: red and green deck rows are interchangeable
steps: Preserve this as the Green Deck child lane, not the parent rollup and not the Red Deck.
Keep local row numbers 001-032 attached to the green deck; do not strip the child-release context.
Do not treat missing rarity symbols as Japanese Base No Rarity proof.
For Pokemon Trader and other sensitive trainer names, require Japanese text/layout comparison before any No Rarity Base claim advances.
When comparing to the parent rollup, retain the source child row id so the same card name does not erase lane provenance.
special_identification_instructions.summary: The Green Deck is a child lane inside Quick Starter; lane membership and missing-symbol caveats must remain visible.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, or binder import says Quick Starter Green Deck, QSGSG, green deck, no-rarity trainer, or one of the Green Deck row names.

narrative.human_title: The green half of the lesson
narrative.why_it_matters: The Green Deck is Quick Starter at its most welcoming: Bulbasaur at the door, little evolution lines, a few strange old Vending memories, then Mewtwo and Chansey waiting deeper in the lane. It feels gentle until the identification work starts. Then it becomes serious, because the same missing-symbol surface that makes these cards feel old can mislead an agent unless the green child lane stays attached to every row.

steps: Preserve the Green Deck child release and row 001.
Do not collapse this row into Base Set Bulbasaur, Expansion Pack Bulbasaur, or the parent rollup without the child lane.
Record Sumiyoshi Kizuki as the local illustrator credit, but do not use artist credit alone as a physical-card identifier.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing or want says Quick Starter Bulbasaur, green deck Bulbasaur, old-back Bulbasaur, or no-rarity Bulbasaur.

narrative.human_title: The green deck begins with a familiar door
narrative.why_it_matters: Bulbasaur at row 001 makes the Green Deck feel immediately legible. Before the traps and the variant talk, the product starts with a starter. Sumiyoshi Kizuki's credit gives this lane its own texture, and the row reminds the agent that even the friendliest opening card still needs its exact release path preserved.

narrative.why_it_matters: Moltres is a small thrill inside the Green Deck. The product is meant to teach, but Arita's legendary bird makes it feel like there is myth hiding inside the lesson. That is the early TCG at its best: practical cardboard that still knows how to make a kid stop and stare.

claims.text: The local catalog identifies row 031 as Pokemon Trader in the Quick Starter Gift Set Green Deck.
The local catalog credits Pokemon Trader 031 to Ken Sugimori.
The local symbol-status matrix lists Pokemon Trader among the explicit Base-overlap trainer trap rows for Quick Starter Gift Set.

Lower-tier collector discussion specifically treats Pokemon Trader as a Quick Starter versus No Rarity comparison problem, supporting row-level text/layout checking before a No Rarity Base claim advances.
Pokemon Trader matters because it carries the Green Deck's strongest identification warning: a missing symbol can look persuasive while still belonging to the wrong assembly history.

steps: Preserve the Green Deck child release and row 031; note that a red-deck Pokemon Trader row also exists.
Do not accept missing rarity symbol alone as Japanese Base No Rarity evidence.
Require side-by-side Japanese text/layout comparison against known Expansion Pack and Quick Starter exemplars before a No Rarity Base Pokemon Trader claim can advance.
Record Ken Sugimori as the local illustrator credit, but do not use artist credit alone as a physical-card identifier.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Pokemon Trader 031 is the Green Deck version of a named Quick Starter text-layout trap.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, or slab label says Pokemon Trader, No Rarity, Quick Starter, QSS, Green Deck, or missing rarity symbol.

narrative.human_title: The green lane's quiet little trapdoor
narrative.why_it_matters: Pokemon Trader is where the Green Deck stops being gentle and starts being forensic. It is just a trainer card until somebody calls it No Rarity. Then the whole protocol wakes up: text layout, row lane, release history, and proof burden all matter. This is exactly the kind of card an agent should love, because it turns confusion into a clean question.
